topic: Exact fixed-parameter optimization of Zhu et al.'s second-order spatial cluster-design risk. For a finite connected graph G, fixed K>=2, closed one-hop exposure neighborhoods, and rational symmetric PSD entrywise-nonnegative pilot covariance Sigma with positive trace, minimize the exact p=1/2 oracle residual criterion V(C;Sigma)=N^-1 sum_{i,i'} 2^{m_ii'(C)+1} Sigma_ii' 1{m_ii'>0} over nonempty G-connected K-partitions. Define the interaction graph F by adding G's edges and clique-completing every scope N[i] union N[i'] with nonzero Sigma_ii'. Prove an exact general MILP and, given a width-w nice tree decomposition of F, a sound-complete DP with bag labels, processed-edge connectivity partitions, and completed-label flags; give a conservative explicit FPT runtime, reconstruct the optimum, and output a rational table/backpointer certificate. Verify the C4 surrogate reversal with exact risks 33.04 versus 38.72, and prove the ordered-entry l1 pilot perturbation and true-design regret bounds. Position against Zhu et al. arXiv:2505.20130 and use Holtz et al.'s Airbnb pricing meta-experiment as consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A processed component of an unfinished label must meet the current bag; forgetting its sole remaining block closes the label, which then cannot restart. At joins, active connectivity partitions merge by transitive closure and an absent label completed in both children is rejected. Label-refining partitions are bounded by Bell(w+1), so K^(w+1) Bell(w+1) 2^K safely bounds states. Every nonzero-covariance scope is a clique of F, hence occurs in a bag and can be charged once at its highest bag. The exact MILP, C4 values, perturbation constants, dense-covariance loss of practical width, and generic connected-partition DP prior art were checked without finding a collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete the node-by-node soundness and completeness induction, especially the join compatibility rule for absent completed labels and the matching backpointer reconstruction certificate. EARLY KILL TEST: On G=a-c-b, K=2, Sigma=diag(1,0,1), use a width-one nice decomposition joining the leaf branches at bag {c}. With a,b labeled 1 and c labeled 2, reject the state where both children close absent label 1, but accept the separator-active analogue; stop if the DP table does otherwise.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed K, can Zhu et al.'s exact second-order oracle residual criterion be minimized over nonempty connected K-partitions by a general MILP and a certificate-producing FPT algorithm parameterized by the treewidth of the covariance-scope interaction graph?

source_refs.claim: Zhu et al. optimize a graph-cut surrogate and evaluate resulting candidates with the full MSE, rather than exactly optimizing the second-order criterion.
source_refs.author: Jin Zhu, Jingyi Li, Hongyi Zhou, Yinan Lin, Zhenhua Lin, and Chengchun Shi

source_refs.claim: This work gives bounded-treewidth dynamic programming for connected partitions with prescribed sizes, but not covariance-scope risk, exact rational costs, or Zhu et al.'s causal-design objective.
source_refs.author: Katrin Casel, Archontia C. Giannopoulou, and Aikaterini Niklanovits

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exact residual cost depends on the number of distinct cluster labels meeting each covariance scope, so it is not a pairwise cut objective; connectedness simultaneously imposes a global constraint on every label class. Generic connected-partition DPs do not establish the required invariant that every processed component of an unfinished label meets the current bag, nor the join rule rejecting a label completed independently in both children. The decisive proof boundary is a node-by-node soundness and completeness induction, including the width-one a-c-b kill test and backpointer reconstruction, together with once-only charging of clique-contained scopes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact rational MILP and a theorem proving that a width-w nice decomposition supports a sound-complete DP with bag labels, active connectivity partitions, completed-label flags, an explicit FPT runtime, optimal-partition reconstruction, and a checkable table/backpointer certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly couples spatial interference, residual correlation, and the computational problem of choosing clusters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Spatial interference favors co-clustering neighbors -> residual correlation creates competing separation incentives -> the full second-order risk is replaced by a tractable surrogate -> recover exact optimization on structurally tractable interaction graphs.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its nice-tree-decomposition states for connected labeled parts, replacing size bookkeeping with covariance-scope charging and proving introduce, forget, and join transitions by induction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles the same global connected-partition constraint on bounded-treewidth graphs; the new theorem must add the causal objective, closure flags, and rational certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over partition-based connectivity states and their proof invariants for weighted connectivity problems on tree decompositions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required states likewise encode equivalence relations among active bag vertices while minimizing an exactly weighted global objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its exposure-weighted estimator, spatial-dependence CLT, and variance-estimation argument after the exact cluster design is selected.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an inference rung for the same global causal estimand under spatial cluster randomization.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what covariance and exposure-scope conditions does Zhu et al.'s pairwise graph-cut surrogate preserve the ordering of connected partitions induced by the exact second-order risk, and how large can the approximation gap be when those conditions fail?

source_refs.claim: The paper substitutes a graph-cut surrogate for the full MSE during cluster construction and subsequently evaluates the generated candidates using the full criterion.
source_refs.author: Jin Zhu, Jingyi Li, Hongyi Zhou, Yinan Lin, Zhenhua Lin, and Chengchun Shi

source_refs.claim: This work obtains graph-cut and semidefinite formulations for worst-case network-interference design objectives, but does not characterize their ordering relative to Zhu et al.'s exact covariance-scope criterion.
source_refs.author: Davide Viviano and coauthors

open_problems.why_unsolved: The surrogate records pairwise separation, while the exact score applies an exponential weight to the number of distinct labels intersecting an entire exposure scope. Consequently, local pairwise agreement need not preserve global rankings: the supplied C4 witness reports exact risks 33.04 and 38.72 in the opposite order from the surrogate. The literature scan found no theorem identifying a regime of order equivalence, an approximation factor, or a family quantifying the worst possible reversal.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary or sufficient condition theorem for exact-surrogate order equivalence, complemented by a sharp approximation bound or a parameterized counterexample family establishing the maximal reversal gap.

writing_exemplar.why: Its transition from the full risk to a spectral graph-cut objective provides the precise motivation and comparison point.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The exact DR variance criterion is combinatorial -> a pairwise graph-cut surrogate enables scalable clustering -> candidate reranking does not certify global agreement -> characterize when the surrogate is faithful and how badly it can reverse exact risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from its exact residual-covariance expansion and surrogate derivation, retaining the discarded multi-label scope terms to isolate equality and domination conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both compared objectives occur explicitly in the same derivation, so their omitted-term decomposition is the natural route to an order-preservation theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its reductions between interference-design criteria and graph optimization to compare a tractable cut objective against a richer variance objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies structurally analogous machinery for proving when graph-cut optimization represents or approximates a causal-design criterion.

open_problems.open_problem: How stable is the exactly optimal connected spatial cluster design to pilot residual-covariance estimation, and what finite-sample regret guarantee follows from ordered-entry l1 covariance error?

source_refs.claim: The iterative procedure estimates residual covariance and empirically approaches its oracle design, but the displayed theory does not give an exact objective-perturbation or plug-in regret inequality.
source_refs.author: Jin Zhu, Jingyi Li, Hongyi Zhou, Yinan Lin, Zhenhua Lin, and Chengchun Shi

source_refs.claim: Viviano proves pilot-based oracle-regret and inference guarantees for network experiments, but not for connected-partition optimization of Zhu et al.'s exact scope-weighted risk.
source_refs.author: Davide Viviano

open_problems.why_unsolved: Each covariance entry is multiplied by a design-dependent exposure factor that can grow exponentially with the number of labels meeting its scope. Existing empirical oracle comparisons do not provide the uniform Lipschitz envelope over all feasible connected K-partitions needed to turn covariance error into a deterministic score bound. Establishing that envelope is the missing step before the standard two-sided comparison can yield true-design regret.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform inequality bounding |V(C;Sigma_hat)-V(C;Sigma)| by an explicit K-dependent constant times ordered-entry l1 error, followed by a true-risk regret theorem for the plug-in minimizer and a high-probability corollary for a specified pilot covariance estimator.

writing_exemplar.why: Its oracle-versus-estimated covariance workflow supplies the practical motivation and identifies where a finite-sample guarantee is absent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The oracle design depends on unknown residual covariance -> repeated experiments permit pilot estimation -> iterative designs empirically approach the oracle -> quantify exact objective sensitivity and selected-design regret.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the pilot-to-main-experiment proof: establish uniform convergence of the estimated variance criterion, compare its minimizer with the infeasible oracle, and condition inference on the pilot.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems select a network experiment using pilot covariance estimates and require oracle regret rather than nuisance consistency alone.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain its cross-fitted doubly robust estimator and sequential covariance update, adding a deterministic objective-stability lemma and a probability bound for covariance error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the estimator-design pair whose exact connected-partition score is being robustified.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the exact connected-partition residual risk be derived and optimized when cluster treatment uses unequal Bernoulli probability p or complete randomization of exactly r treated clusters rather than independent p=1/2 assignment?

source_refs.claim: Zhu et al. fix independent cluster treatment probability p=0.5, leaving unequal and fixed-count cluster allocation outside their risk and optimization formulas.
source_refs.author: Jin Zhu, Jingyi Li, Hongyi Zhou, Yinan Lin, Zhenhua Lin, and Chengchun Shi

source_refs.claim: Network propagation can make one-half treatment suboptimal for power, so the treatment proportion is itself a substantive design choice.
source_refs.author: Jake Bowers, Bruce A. Desmarais, Mark Frederickson, Nahomi Ichino, Hsuan-Wei Lee, and Simi Wang

source_refs.claim: This paper optimizes correlated assignments for already formed clusters under a common marginal q, not joint connected-partition optimization under Zhu et al.'s exact residual risk.
source_refs.author: Ozan Candogan, Chen Chen, and Rad Niazadeh

open_problems.why_unsolved: The factor depending only on the number of scope labels exploits independent fair cluster coins. Unequal Bernoulli assignment separates treated and control exposure probabilities, whereas exactly-r-of-K assignment creates hypergeometric dependence between scopes. The first proof step that changes is the closed-form covariance of exposure-weighted residual contributions; fixed-count assignment may additionally require global allocation-count bookkeeping that is absent from local scope charging.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Closed-form exact residual-risk functionals for general p and exactly-r-of-K assignment, with a sound-complete MILP or treewidth-parameterized optimizer and a rational optimal-design certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames treatment proportion as a network-design decision controlled by the interference mechanism.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Propagation changes the information supplied by an assignment -> half treatment need not maximize power -> spatial designs should accommodate the allocation law as well as cluster geometry -> derive and optimize exact unequal-p and fixed-count risks.

method_exemplars.technique: Redo the exact DR residual-covariance expansion without substituting p=1/2, tracking treated and control exposure probabilities separately.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination retains the estimand, exposure mapping, and connected partition class while changing only the cluster assignment law.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its covariance-level formulation for cluster assignments with prescribed marginal probability and its worst-case variance comparison.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides machinery for nonstandard cluster-level allocation laws even though cluster construction is fixed in that paper.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its exposure-weighted estimator, assignment-based dependence analysis, CLT, and variance estimator to unequal or fixed-count cluster allocation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives a complete inference layer for global effects under spatial cluster randomization.

open_problems.open_problem: Can Zhu et al.'s exact covariance-aware design criterion be reformulated for bipartite marketplaces and exactly optimized over connected seller clusters when buyer-mediated spillovers include both substitution and complementarity?

source_refs.claim: The Airbnb meta-experiment finds substantial interference bias while identifying cluster-randomization power loss and interventions with mixed demand directions as limitations.
source_refs.author: David Holtz, Felipe Lobel, Ruben Lobel, Inessa Liskovich, and Sinan Aral

source_refs.claim: This paper maps bipartite experiment design to correlation clustering, but does not exactly optimize a covariance-aware doubly robust residual criterion over connected clusters.
source_refs.author: Jean Pouget-Abadie, Kevin Aydin, Warren Schudy, Kay Brodersen, and Vahab Mirrokni

source_refs.claim: Zhu et al.'s covariance-aware criterion uses one-hop spatial neighborhoods rather than buyer-mediated bipartite exposure scopes.
source_refs.author: Jin Zhu, Jingyi Li, Hongyi Zhou, Yinan Lin, Zhenhua Lin, and Chengchun Shi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Airbnb interference is mediated through buyer consideration sets, so assignment units and outcome-relevant exposure units do not coincide. Bipartite correlation clustering captures exposure variation but not Zhu et al.'s covariance-weighted DR residual risk, while mixed substitution and complementarity can invalidate the entrywise-nonnegative local-cost argument. The first altered proof step is the construction of exposure scopes and their interaction graph; the subsequent obstacle is determining conditions under which signed contributions still permit exact local charging and bounded-treewidth optimization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-population bipartite exposure model with an exact covariance-aware DR risk formula, sufficient conditions for connected-cluster MILP/FPT optimization despite mixed-sign spillovers, and an estimator with a design-based limit or coverage theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: Its marketplace meta-experiment and discussion of interference, power loss, and mixed demand responses provide the closest destination-side formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Buyer choice links competing listings -> seller-level Bernoulli tests suffer interference bias -> cluster randomization reduces bias but loses power and relies on monotone demand movement -> design exact covariance-aware clusters for signed bipartite spillovers.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the folding of a bipartite diversion-outcome graph into a clustering objective, replacing correlation weights with exact covariance-scope contributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the structural map from marketplace bipartite exposure sets to a partition objective.

method_exemplars.technique: Use generalized propensity scores for bipartite exposures to construct effect estimators and confidence sets with design-correct coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides estimation and inference when treatment-assignment units differ from outcome units.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the residual-covariance decomposition of the doubly robust estimator and determine which terms survive under buyer-mediated exposure scopes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed criterion is explicitly a bipartite analogue of Zhu et al.'s second-order risk.

literature_map:
Zhu et al. (2025, ICML, arXiv:2505.20130) derive a covariance-aware DR MSE decomposition but construct clusters by optimizing a spectral graph-cut surrogate.
Leung (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2111.04219) proves rate-optimal spatial cluster designs, asymptotic normality, and variance estimation under decaying interference.
Viviano et al. (2023, arXiv:2310.14983) reduce worst-case network-interference design to graph-cut and semidefinite computations, not exact covariance-scope optimization.
Viviano (2026, JPE Microeconomics, arXiv:2003.08421) uses pilot estimates of network variance and covariance and proves design-regret and inference guarantees.
Ugander et al. (2013, KDD, arXiv:1305.6979) establish graph cluster randomization, exposure-probability computation, and Horvitz-Thompson unbiasedness.
Ugander and Yin (2023, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:2009.02297) randomize graph clusterings to repair fixed-partition exposure pathologies.
Eckles, Karrer, and Ugander (2017, Journal of Causal Inference, doi:10.1515/jci-2015-0021) frame graph clustering as bias reduction under network interference.
Aronow and Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics) provide the exposure-mapping identification and design-based estimation framework.
Candogan, Chen, and Niazadeh (2023, Management Science, doi:10.1287/mnsc.2021.02741) optimize correlated treatment assignments for existing clusters under a common marginal probability.
Chen, Li, Deng, and Wang (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2311.14042) optimize treatment covariance under one-hop interference using a projected-gradient heuristic and an MSE upper bound.
Bowers et al. (2018, Social Networks, arXiv:1609.00923) show that network propagation can make one-half treatment suboptimal for power.
Holtz et al. (2024, Management Science, arXiv:2004.12489) document Airbnb pricing interference and highlight cluster-design power loss and mixed demand shifts.
Pouget-Abadie et al. (2019, NeurIPS) formulate bipartite experiment design as correlation clustering; Doudchenko et al. (2020, arXiv:2010.02108) develop bipartite estimation and coverage.
Bodlaender et al. (2015, Information and Computation, arXiv:1211.1505) provide partition-state machinery for weighted connectivity problems on bounded-treewidth graphs.
Casel, Giannopoulou, and Niklanovits (2026, arXiv:2607.22070) give a generic bounded-treewidth DP for connected partitions, but not Zhu et al.'s exact risk, rational reconstruction certificate, or pilot-perturbation bounds.
